nodes.name: Rapid Self-Exothermic Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Ruthenium-coupled RE-OCl heterogeneous catalysts Ru/REOCl (RE = Pr, Nd, Sm) were prepared by a rapid self-exothermic method following sol-gel process. The highly exothermic nature provides sufficient energy to overcome the barrier of lattice mismatch and promote the formation of highly coupled interfaces between Ru and REOCl. The extremely short reaction time leads the rapid nucleation of metallic Ru nanoparticles (<4 nm), but limits the further growth. After the sol-gel process and a few-seconds reaction with large heat release reaching thousands of degrees Celsius instantaneously, the black Ru/REOCl powders could be collected. Ru/NdOCl with optimized Ru/Nd molar ratio of 2:1 was used as example (detailed in Note S1, Table S1, Figures S1-S4).

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM confirms high density of uniformly sized Ru nanocrystals with average diameter <4 nm embedded within continuous matrix.
nodes.evidence_snippet: high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HR-TEM, Figure 1c) image also confirmed a high density of uniformly sized Ru nanocrystals, with an average diameter of less than 4 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM with FFT/IFFT shows Ru (001) plane at 2.33 Å and NdOCl (102) plane at 2.55 Å with atomic-level amorphous layer connecting them.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding fast Fourier transform (FFT) and the inverse FFT (IFFT) patterns showed that the d1 and d2 regions were assigned to the Ru (0 0 1) and NdOCl (1 0 2) planes, with average interplanar spacings of 2.33 and 2.55Å

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM-EDS elemental mapping shows Cl distribution overlaps more with Ru than Nd and O, indicating Cl bridge formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both elemental mapping analyses indicated that the Cl distribution exhibited a greater overlap with elemental Ru compared to those of Nd and O.

nodes.characterization_summary: EELS elemental mapping confirms Cl-Ru association consistent with EDS results.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Enfina electron energy loss spectroscopy (EELS, Figure 1f) maps for the Ru/NdOCl composites. Both elemental mapping analyses indicated that the Cl distribution...

nodes.characterization_summary: Nd L3-edge EXAFS shows slightly shortened Nd-O coordination, increased Nd-Cl bond intensity, and decreased Nd…Nd bonds compared to pure NdOCl.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with the pure NdOCl crystals, the Nd-O coordination kept the similar state but slightly shortened R position in Nd L3-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra

nodes.characterization_summary: High-resolution XPS: Cl 2p shifts to higher energy in Ru/NdOCl with Cl_strong peaks disappeared; O 1s splits to O-M (529.68 eV) and O_weak (532.05 eV) from 531.48 eV lattice oxygen.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution Cl 2p spectrum of NdOCl... In the case of Ru/NdOCl, the overall peak position of Cl 2p was shifted to a high energy region, and the Cl_strong coupled peaks disappeared.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge EXAFS shows new WT intensity at 1.68 Å corresponding to Ru-Cl/O bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ru—Cl/O bond was reconfirmed by Ru K-edge EXAFS spectra analysis... contributed to the newly-formed WT intensity at a path length of 1.68Å

nodes.characterization_summary: EPR shows higher oxygen/chlorine vacancies in Ru/NdOCl (1.233×10¹³ spins g⁻¹) than NdOCl (7.925×10¹² spins g⁻¹).
nodes.evidence_snippet: more oxygen and/or chlorine vacancies appeared in Ru/NdOCl (1.233×10¹³ spins g⁻¹) compared with that in the pure NdOCl (7.925×10¹² spins g⁻¹)

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ adsorption-desorption and BJH analysis confirm enriched mesopores of 11 nm diameter and BET surface area of 18.63 m² g⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: N₂ adsorption-desorption measurements and the corresponding Barrett-Joyner-Halenda analysis... confirmed that Ru/NdOCl owned the enriched mesopores with the diameter of 11 nm and a large Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 18.63 m² g⁻¹

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru K-edge XANES shows edge close to Ru foil; Ru valency +0.13 in Ru/NdOCl (lower than +0.43 in Ru powder).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectra (XANES, Figure 3d) showed that the adsorption edges of Ru/NdOCl was very close to the reference Ru foil... The Ru (+0.13) in Ru/NdOCl exhibited lower valence state than Ru powder (+0.43)

nodes.characterization_summary: UPS reveals work function of 5.1 eV for Ru/NdOCl (increased vs Ru powder).
nodes.evidence_snippet: UV photo-electron spectroscopy (UPS) was conducted (Figure 3c), revealing an increased work function of 5.1 eV for Ru/NdOCl compared to that of Ru powder

nodes.characterization_summary: Ru 3p peaks in Ru/NdOCl shift to lower binding energy (461.73, 483.89 eV) vs Ru powder.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the doublet peaks of Ru⁰ 3p₃/₂ and 3p₁/₂ in Ru/NdOCl (at 461.73 and 483.89 eV, respectively) shifted to lower binding energy compared to Ru powder

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows obvious macropores on lamellar texture and nanoscale metallic particles socketed in porous layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru/NdOCl indeed presented the obvious macropores on the lamellar texture shown in scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images (Figure S5a, Supporting Information)
